aboutH2: About Recovery Alberta Child, Youth and Family Services in Medicine Hat
intro: Recovery Alberta's Child, Youth and Family service in Medicine Hat (formerly Alberta Health Services Youth Counselling) offers a range of treatment services to help Albertans improve their health, learn new life skills and recover from the harmful effects of substance use and problem gambling. The range of services includes screening, assessment, individual and group counseling, referral to other resources, and aftercare support. Assessment and treatment will include learning about your past history, and present situation and identifying your goals.

pillars.title: An Outpatient Office in Downtown Medicine Hat
pillars.body: Counselling takes place in Room 01 of the Medicine Hat Provincial Building at 346 3 Street SE. This is an outpatient office, so young people come in for appointments and go home afterwards. Other Recovery Alberta services work from the same building, among them adult community addiction counselling and child and youth mental health, which helps when a family needs more than one kind of support.

pillars.title: Aftercare Support and Where to Go Next
pillars.body: Aftercare support and referrals to other resources are part of the service. When weekly counselling isn't enough, staff can refer a young person to the child and youth day program or to the urgent mental health and addiction team (UMAT). Adults in the family can use the community addiction service down the hall, and the Medicine Hat Recovery Centre on Kipling Street SE provides adult detox and residential treatment.

pillars.title: Counsellors and Therapists Who Work With Families
pillars.body: The team is made up of addiction counsellors and mental health therapists, and a nurse practitioner is available by referral. Parents and caregivers can join sessions through family counselling, and the service also offers a youth and family mobile option. Staff give information about alcohol, drugs, tobacco and gambling to anyone who asks, including health providers and employers.

overviewH2: Recovery Alberta in Medicine Hat: Service Overview
overview: The counselor will talk with you about the different treatment options, including counseling to help you reach your goals. Your counselor will help you choose goals and strategies, make suggestions, and review your progress with you.
With integrated core values of empathy, transformation, connection, curiosity, and acceptance, we help children, teens and families with psychological counsel services (groups & workshops).

location.heading: Recovery Alberta Child, Youth and Family Services in Medicine Hat, Alberta
location.intro: The service is in downtown Medicine Hat, in Room 01 of the Provincial Building at 346 3 Street SE. From downtown Calgary it's about 3 hours east on the Trans-Canada Highway; Lethbridge is roughly 1 hour 45 minutes away, Brooks a little over an hour, and Redcliff about 10 minutes.

faqIntro: Answers come from Recovery Alberta's listing in the provincial service directory and the original listing. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is this youth counselling service in Medicine Hat or Calgary?
faqs.a: It is in Medicine Hat. The office is in Room 01 of the Medicine Hat Provincial Building at 346 3 Street SE, T1A 0G7. An older version of this listing gave a Calgary address by mistake; the service has no Calgary location.

Recovery Alberta runs it. Addiction and mental health services moved from Alberta Health Services to Recovery Alberta on September 1, 2024, and this service, once called Addiction Services Youth Counselling, is now listed as Addiction and Mental Health: Child, Youth and Family.

faqs.q: How do I get an appointment?
faqs.a: Parents and young people can self-refer by calling Access Addiction and Mental Health at 1-888-594-0211, for mental health therapy, addictions counselling or the youth and family mobile service. Other providers can also refer. The nurse practitioner, the child and youth day program and UMAT need a referral.
Yes, on Thursday and Friday between 12:00 and 3:15 pm for a single session walk-in. No referral is needed. For anything else, call 403-529-3582 or the self-referral line first.

This is a public service run by Recovery Alberta, not a private clinic, and no fees are published. The Alberta government says publicly funded addiction treatment is free for Albertans. Call 403-529-3582 to confirm what you'll need to bring; the adult service in the same building asks for an Alberta Health Care card and photo ID.

The office is open Monday, Wednesday and Friday from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, and Tuesday and Thursday from 8:00 am to 7:15 pm. It is closed on weekends. Outside those hours, the 24-hour Addiction Helpline is 1-866-332-2322.

faqs.q: Where is it and how do I get there from Calgary?
faqs.a: The Provincial Building is at 346 3 Street SE in downtown Medicine Hat. From Calgary, it's about a 3-hour drive east on the Trans-Canada Highway (Highway 1), passing Brooks on the way. From Lethbridge, allow about 1 hour 45 minutes.

faqs.q: Does it offer detox or residential treatment?
faqs.a: No, this is an outpatient counselling service. In Medicine Hat, adult detox and residential treatment are at the Medicine Hat Recovery Centre, 370 Kipling Street SE, which runs 24 hours and can be reached at 403-529-9021.

faqs.q: Is there help for adults in the same building?
faqs.a: Yes. Recovery Alberta's Community Addiction Services, office #2 in the same building, sees people of all ages and can be reached at 403-529-3500. It runs regular drop-in times and booked appointments, with a listed wait of 7 to 21 days, and anyone under 18 needs parental consent.

Aftercare support and referrals to other resources are part of the service. Your counsellor reviews progress with you and can connect you to the day program, UMAT or adult services if more help is needed.
Call 911 in an emergency. The Addiction Helpline at 1-866-332-2322 answers 24 hours a day, 211 Alberta connects you to local services at any hour, and 988 is the Suicide Crisis Helpline.
